title: My Plans After Graduation
writingModel: My Plans After Graduation — by Amir Bekzhanov

I'm going to graduate from WKU in June, and I already know what comes next. I've been offered a position at a tech startup in Almaty — a small team of fifteen people working on artificial intelligence integration. I'm going to start work in July, just a few weeks after graduation. It's all moving quite quickly, and honestly, I'm excited.

The startup is small by design. I could have applied to large corporations — several of my friends are going to join companies with hundreds of employees. But I think I'll learn more in a smaller environment. I'll have more responsibility, more variety, and more direct contact with the product itself. In a large company, I'd probably spend my first year doing one specific task. At the startup, I'll be involved in multiple areas from day one.

In the short term, my main goal is to prove myself during the first six months. I'm going to work as hard as I can and show the team that they made the right decision. I'll also try to improve my spoken English — I'm good at reading and writing, but I need to be more confident in meetings. I'm going to attend an online conversation course while I'm working.

In the long term, I'm not entirely sure what direction I want to go. I think I'll stay in technology — it's what I know and love. But I might move into product management rather than pure coding. I'll see how the first year goes before making any big decisions.

There is one thing I'm certain about: I'm not going to stop learning. I'm going to read books about leadership, technology, and business. I'll probably sign up for some online courses in the evenings. My parents are happy with my plans — they always said that the most important thing is to keep moving forward. I think they're right.
